recognize_zh: 視野下方中央一顆紅血球內布滿大量粗大、深藍色的點狀顆粒且分布於整個細胞，即粗大嗜鹼性點彩（coarse basophilic stippling）；背景紅血球大小不一、低色素並有標靶細胞，符合重型乙型地中海貧血。
features: Single red cell containing numerous coarse, dark blue punctate granules distributed throughout the cell
Granules are uniform in color and scattered diffusely rather than clustered at the periphery
Background red cells show anisocytosis, poikilocytosis and hypochromia
Target cells and irregularly shaped red cells are present
Occasional small platelets; no nucleated red cells in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows marked anisopoikilocytosis with hypochromic red cells, target cells, and irregular forms. In the lower center of the field, a red cell contains numerous coarse, dark blue granules distributed throughout the cytoplasm, representing coarse basophilic stippling (aggregated ribosomal RNA). No malarial parasites or Pappenheimer body clusters are evident. Findings are consistent with coarse basophilic stippling in the setting of dyserythropoiesis, such as beta-thalassemia major; lead poisoning and pyrimidine 5'-nucleotidase deficiency should be considered if clinically appropriate.

ddx.vs: Pappenheimer bodies are fewer, small clustered granules at the cell periphery that stain with Prussian blue, whereas basophilic stippling is diffuse and iron-negative.
Lead poisoning produces morphologically identical coarse stippling, so blood lead level and clinical history are needed to separate it.
Parasites show ring forms with chromatin dots and cytoplasm or Maltese crosses rather than numerous uniform punctate granules.
Howell-Jolly bodies are usually a single larger round dense nuclear remnant rather than many fine to coarse dots.
